faq.q: What does feeling proud feel like?
faq.a: Pride is a warm, happy glow inside, often in your chest. You might smile, stand taller and want to tell someone about what you did.

faq.q: Is it okay to feel proud of myself?
faq.a: Yes! Feeling proud of your hard work, kindness or bravery is healthy and helps you keep trying.

faq.q: Can I be proud even if I did not win?
faq.a: Absolutely. You can be proud of trying your best, practising, getting better or being a good team mate, whatever the result.
asks: Can I be proud of trying?

faq.q: What is the difference between pride and showing off?
faq.a: Pride is a warm feeling about what you did. Showing off is boasting or putting others down. You can share good news proudly without making others feel small.
asks: Is being proud the same as boasting?

faq.q: How can I help someone else feel proud?
faq.a: Notice their effort and tell them, like "You practised so hard, and it worked!" Saying exactly what they did well makes it special.
asks: How do I praise a friend?

facts: Studies by psychologist Jessica Tracy found that the proud pose, with head tilted up and chest out, is recognised in many cultures, including remote villages in Burkina Faso.
Athletes who were blind from birth, and had never seen anyone make the pose, still raised their arms and lifted their chins after winning.
